title: observability: token-level KV/cost/latency dashboards + alert tuning + tracing enhancements
author: Aisha Malhotra
description:
Motivation: production teams need per-token visibility (cost + latency) and better KV cache observability to diagnose regressions and control inference unit economics. This PR adds token-level metrics for KV cache hit/miss, token cost attribution panels, improved tracing spans separating prefix vs generation phases, dashboard panels, and tuned alert rules to reduce noise while catching cost/latency regressions.

What this includes: checklist:
- [x] Prometheus collectors for kv_cache_hit_total / kv_cache_miss_total and token_cost_seconds (cost attribution by token)
- [x] OpenTelemetry tracing spans for request phases: receive -> prefix_lookup -> generation -> post_process (adds resource attributes: model_id, shard, queueing_ms)
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON: observability/grafana/dashboards/token_kv_cost.json (panels for cost-per-token, median/95/99 latency split by token phase)
- [x] Alert rules: token-cost-spike, token-tail-latency, kv-cache-degradation with tuned thresholds and suppression windows
- [x] CI e2e observations test and unit tests for metric formatting
- [x] Docs: docs/observability/token-metrics.md with migration notes and runbook links

Implementation notes: the metric names follow conventions used elsewhere in the repo (prefix redwood_). Token cost is computed at emit time using per-token CPU/GPU microcost estimates + egress/ingest multipliers; we store a dimensioned histogram and a derived PromQL recording rule for cost per 1k tokens. Tracing adds light-weight span attributes and avoids heavy baggage to keep ingestion costs down. We added low-frequency log sampling (1%) for verbose request logs and a flag to opt-in per-customer during debugging.

Related linear tasks: ENG-2345 (token metrics), ENG-2390 (kv cache observability). This PR is intentional about keeping telemetry cardinality limited: limited label sets (model_id, region, capacity_tier) and bounded cardinality for shard tags.

Migration/rollout: dashboards and alerts are staged to staging first, then promoted. The feature is behind a feature-flag (obs.token_kv_cost) enabled for internal staging and a canary set of customers. See docs/observability/token-metrics.md for rollback steps and runbooks.

Add OpenTelemetry spans + resource attributes for request phases
Create Grafana dashboard JSON for token_kv_cost panels
Add Prometheus recording rules and alerting YAML for token-cost and kv-cache
Add CI e2e observability test and update ci matrix
Docs: add token-metrics.md and runbook links
review_conversation: Carlos Nguyen: Please add a unit test for the recording rule semantics; current PromQL in recording_rules.yaml looks like it will double-count when used with batch aggregation.
Aisha Malhotra: Added tests + clarified PromQL in 3rd commit; recording rule now uses sum without double aggregation and has a comment explaining the rationale.
Priya Shah: Can we reduce cardinality further by dropping shard tag from dashboard panels? Shard helps debugging but causes grafana row explosion.
Aisha Malhotra: Kept shard as an optional breakdown (panel variable) but removed it from default group_by. Updated dashboard JSON and docs to note how to opt-in to shard dimension.
Blake Turner: LGTM pending CI green and a short note in the runbook about alert escalation to infra on persistent kv miss rate > 5%

release_notes:
- Added token-level KV cache metrics (redwood_kv_cache_hit_total / redwood_kv_cache_miss_total)
- Added token cost attribution metric and Grafana dashboard with cost/latency breakdowns by token phase
- Improved tracing spans for prefix vs generation phases (adds model_id, queueing_ms)
- Tuned alerts for token-cost spikes, kv-cache degradation, and token-tail-latency with suppression windows
- Log sampling (1%) to reduce verbose log ingestion; opt-in per-customer debugging
